The OpenDataPhilly listing covers every Philly311 service and information request since December 8, 2014, whether submitted through the app, phone, walk-ins, email, the website, or social media ([opendataphilly.org](https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/)). The city describes the dataset as very large and suggests using its visualization unless you're comfortable with the Carto SQL API ([opendataphilly.org](https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/)).

Other details:
- **Downloads:** Files are split by year, with CSV and SHP formats for 2014 through 2025 listed on the Data.gov mirror ([catalog-beta.data.gov](https://catalog-beta.data.gov/dataset/311-service-and-information-requests)). The full CSV or SHP files can fail to download, so the city recommends the API for the complete set ([geo.btaa.org](https://geo.btaa.org/catalog/0c0cf472-51ae-4a97-bb97-97f773af9c61)).
- **Update frequency and license:** The listing says it updates daily and is under the City of Philadelphia License. The maintainer contact is 311datarequest@phila.gov ([opendataphilly.org](https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/)).
- **Content:** The data records two kinds of entries, service requests and information requests. A service request is a need the city would fulfill, such as a pothole repair or graffiti removal ([phila.gov](https://www.phila.gov/press-releases/mayor/city-optimizes-citizen-access-to-philly311-data/)).

The City of Houston publishes its 311 request data mainly through its ArcGIS REST services, and the results point to two main layers.

- **Archived/full 311 dataset:** The "Houston311_Service_Requests" layer covers publicly available requests from the LAGAN system and is updated monthly. It excludes animal-related (BARC) tickets, which live in a separate system, so it's meant to be paired with the public BARC location layer. Monthly update from Lagan is noted in its metadata, and it allows JSON, GeoJSON, and PBF query formats with a 2,000-record cap per request. Its coordinates use the NAD 1983 StatePlane Texas South Central (feet) projection.
- **Recent requests layer:** The "Houston311 Recent Service Requests" layer includes open cases plus closed cases from the past two weeks, refreshed every 30 minutes.
- **Field definitions:** The service's column descriptions include fields such as the case number, council district, neighborhood, service area, and department, plus the HCAD tax ID for the location. These descriptions come from an ArcGIS services directory page for a related flood-event layer.
- **City data portal:** The city's open data portal at data.houstontx.gov hosts City of Houston datasets, though the search results didn't show a specific 311 entry there.

I didn't find a current, verified link to a single downloadable 311 CSV on the portal, so check data.houstontx.gov directly for that. The ABC13 article from December 2025 also reports that the city runs a dashboard that tracks and grades 311 service requests, which may be a useful companion resource.

The main dataset appears to be the 311 Service Requests set on the City of Chicago portal, identifier **v6vf-nfxy** (homepage: data.cityofchicago.org/d/v6vf-nfxy). I could only reach third-party catalog mirrors (data.gov), not the portal itself, so the details below are as those mirrors report them.

- **Scope:** The dataset holds requests logged since the new 311 system went live, plus some older records flagged in a LEGACY_RECORD column. Records from the previous system are indicated in the LEGACY_RECORD column.
- **Location caveat:** Location fields for "311 INFORMATION ONLY CALL" requests often show the address of the City's 311 Center, not the caller's location (requests of the type 311 INFORMATION ONLY CALL often are entered with the address of the City's 311 Center).
- **Freshness and access:** One mirror shows a last-modified date of April 12, 2026, and lists the data as public with no license information provided.
- **Older datasets:** Several historical sets were superseded by v6vf-nfxy. For example, the vacant and abandoned buildings set is marked historical-only, and its function moved to v6vf-nfxy (the function of this dataset was replaced by v6vf-nfxy). The sanitation code complaints set (me59-5fac) carries the same note.
- **Related sets:** The garbage carts dataset (9ksk-na4q) is updated daily, and duplicate entries are marked with "Open - Dup" or "Completed - Dup" in the Status field.

content.text:
I confirmed four of the six cities on the portals themselves. LA is only partly confirmed, and Houston's field name and start year are not confirmed.

| City | Dataset URL | Platform | Update frequency as stated | Earliest year | Closure field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NYC | https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/erm2-nwe9 ("311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present") | Socrata | Daily | 2020 (2010–2019 is a separate dataset) | `closed_date` |
| Los Angeles | https://data.lacity.org/d/ndkd-k878 ("MyLA311 Service Request Data 2016") | Socrata | Weekly | 2016 | `closeddate` |
| Chicago | https://data.cityofchicago.org/d/v6vf-nfxy ("311 Service Requests") | Socrata | "Multiple times per day" | 2018 | `closed_date` |
| Houston | Houston311_Service_Requests layer, `mycity2.houstontx.gov/pubgis01/rest/services/311/311_ARCHIVED_CASES/MapServer/0` | ArcGIS | Monthly (from the Lagan system) | Unverified | Unverified |
| Philadelphia | https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/ | CKAN-style catalog; data served through Carto's SQL API (table `public_cases_fc`) | Daily | 2014 | `closed_datetime` |
| San Francisco | https://data.sf.gov/d/vw6y-z8j6 ("311 Cases") | Socrata | Multiple times per hour (publishing frequency "Daily"; description says nightly) | 2008 (from 7/1/2008) | `closed_date` |

**NYC:** The dataset ID `erm2-nwe9` used to cover 2010 to present. It now holds only 2020 onward, so 2010–2019 records are in a separate dataset I didn't look up.

**Los Angeles:**
- LA publishes one dataset per year, so you'd need to combine them. I only retrieved the 2016 one.
- I didn't find the datasets for later years.
- The 2013–2014 dataset (`bpyg-ytsg`) is call-center statistics, not service requests.
- I assumed the field name is the same in the later years, but I didn't check.
- The metadata notes `closeddate` is not used by all request types.

**Chicago:** The dataset says it covers requests since the new 311 system launched on 12/18/2018. It also has some legacy records, and the earliest `created_date` is in July 2018. The v6vf-nk8k ID I first guessed returned 404.

**Houston:**
- Its 311 data is served from ArcGIS REST services. I couldn't find a 311 request dataset on the CKAN portal at data.houstontx.gov. It only lists the Lagan knowledge dump and BARC animal requests.
- The archived-cases service was offline (HTTP 500, "not started") when I tried it, so I couldn't read its fields or date range.
- There is also a "Recent Service Requests" layer, which holds open cases plus cases closed in the last two weeks and refreshes every 30 minutes.
- The archived layer excludes animal (BARC) tickets.
